title: OC Sport, France's sport-sector certification body, says an unauthorized party accessed its certification platform from 21 October to 12 November
date_note: Day OC Sport posted its notice (the site's own post date, 20 November 2026; the page itself shows no date). The notice says access ran from 21 October to 12 November 2026, was found on 12 November, and the CNIL was informed on 16 November.
org: Organisme Certificateur de la branche du Sport (OC Sport)
geo_basis: registered address on OC Sport's legal notice page (88 rue Marcel Bourdarias, 94140 Alfortville)
summary: OC Sport, the certification body of France's sport sector, says unauthorized access to its certification management platform was found on 12 November 2026 and ran from 21 October. Names, birth details, contact details and diploma (parchemin) numbers of 2026 candidates and certified people were involved, some files with ID or medical certificate copies. OC Sport says it cannot rule out that the data was viewed or copied, and informed the CNIL on 16 November.
plain: The body that issues France's sport-sector professional certificates says someone got into its certification platform between 21 October and 12 November. Personal details of 2026 candidates, and in some files ID or medical certificate copies, may have been viewed or copied.
exec: Confirmed unauthorized access to a certification platform; some files held identity or medical certificate copies, and OC Sport cannot rule out the data was viewed or copied.
action: OC Sport urges people who get suspicious messages not to reply or click any link, and says it never asks for a password or an identity document by email.
impact: Candidates and certified people of the sport sector's 2026 certifications (CQP, TFP, CCP).

report.publisher: Organisme Certificateur de la branche du Sport (OC Sport)
key_findings: Unauthorized access to OC Sport's certification management platform was found on 12 November 2026; it ran from 21 October to 12 November 2026.

Data involved: name, first name, date and place of birth, email address, phone number and certificate number of certified people; some files could also contain a copy of an identity document or a medical certificate.
OC Sport says it cannot be excluded that the data was viewed or copied by an unauthorized third party; the CNIL was informed on 16 November 2026.
recommendations: Do not reply to suspicious messages or click any link; OC Sport never asks for a password or identity document by email.

evidence.quote: Cet accès s’est étendu du 21 octobre au 12 novembre 2026.
La CNIL a été informée de cette violation le 16 novembre 2026.

validation.note: Primary: OC Sport's own notice on ocsport.org (posted 20 November 2026). Also reported by cyberattaque.org on 23 November 2026, which relays the notice.
